Before pushing, check last_notified_trigger: if the SAME trigger is still the live one and nothing material has changed, DO NOT notify again -- update the timestamp and mark and stay silent. Re-notify only when a DIFFERENT trigger fires, a fired trigger un-fires, or the recommendation itself changes. A position quietly working is not news; the journal and the EOD report already carry it.

durable_findings.the_first_large_UPWARD_1_minute_revision:
MEASURED 2026-08-26T15:32Z, and it completes today's 14:31Z finding from the opposite direction. That earlier run proved 1-minute bars are revised after they close (a -95.5% volume revision with a changed OHLC) and noted revisions 'ran both up and down' without having measured a large up-side case. It carries the exact signature the rule teaches: a bar whose volume is a tiny fraction of BOTH neighbours (7,968 and 22,840) is PROVISIONAL, not a quiet minute. Three other bars in the same window revised materially (15:14 -13.9%, 15:18 +10.7%, 15:26 -4.7%), so this is a live property of the feed, not a one-off.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE NEW LESSON, AND IT IS A HOLE IN THE EXISTING FIX. The 'end the trailing baseline ~10 minutes back' rule protects the DENOMINATOR and nothing else. A provisional bar in the last minutes of the CANDIDATE window sits inside the numerator and outside a baseline that already ended ten minutes ago, so its revision is ONE-SIDED by construction. Measured exactly here: the revision moved the candidate 5-minute bar +28.6% (37,572 -> 48,331) while moving the baseline -0.11% (94,849 -> 94,749), lifting the confirmation reading from 39.7% to 51.0% of baseline. That is the FALSE-POSITIVE direction -- the same dangerous direction as the dropped-bucket defect, arriving through the opposite mechanism.

THE FIX, symmetric with the one already in the playbook: the final bar of a candidate window is the single bar most likely to be provisional AND the one whose revision cannot be offset. So either end the CANDIDATE window ~10 minutes back as well, or double-read its constituent minutes before letting it confirm. This run did the latter -- two fetches a minute apart, merged, disagreements resolved to the later read.

HONEST SCOPE, and it is what makes the audit credible: this changed NO decision today. The price clause failed outright, and 51% of baseline still fails the volume clause decisively. A filter's inputs can only be audited honestly on a day the correction does not flip the answer -- and the uncorrected 39.7% would have supported a stronger 'volume has collapsed' claim than the data actually carries, which is the small dishonesty this catch prevents.

volume_clause_denominator_collapse.title: A TRAILING-LOCAL VOLUME BASELINE INVERTS IN A DECAYING TAPE: THE CLAUSE GETS EASIER EXACTLY WHERE IT SHOULD GET HARDER. Measured 2026-08-26T15:52Z on the session's first clean bullish fire.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.measurement: QQQ 15:40-15:44Z candidate bucket = 98,957 shares (read B; read A 100,833, agreeing within 1.9%). Against the settled trailing-30-ending-10-back baseline of 66,144 it reads 149.6% and CONFIRMS. Against the same session's own earlier baselines it reads 80.1% (13:45-14:14, 123,470), 84.8% (14:05-14:34, 116,660), 83.9% (the 117,990 that today's 15:00Z fire cleared at 209.6%) and 39.8% of the actual 14:25Z flush bucket (248,511). The same absolute volume fails the clause at 13:45Z and passes it at 15:40Z, on a tape where participation fell rather than rose.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.mechanism: The 2026-08-25 calibration rule correctly replaced a session-average denominator with a trailing-local one, because the opening hour's 254,448/bar made midday fires impossible. That fix is right and stays. What nobody checked is the other end: a trailing-local mean tracks a DECAYING tape downward, so as participation drains the bar to clear falls with it. In a pre-event vacuum the clause stops asking 'did participation arrive' and starts asking 'is this bar busier than the vacuum' -- which any drift back toward normal satisfies. The filter is self-fulfilling exactly when the tape is least informative.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.why_it_survived: Both denominator defects are invisible from outcomes and point in OPPOSITE directions, so neither is detectable by counting fires. A session-average baseline vetoes everything and looks like discipline; a collapsed local baseline confirms everything and looks like the filter finally working. The 15:30Z run predicted a clean fire would FAIL on volume and treated a volume-confirmed break as 'far more informative than usual' -- exactly backwards, and it was refuted fifteen minutes later. A run that inherits that framing reads a vacuum fire as high-conviction.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.detector: Report the candidate bar's volume in ABSOLUTE terms alongside the ratio, and test it against the session's OWN earlier baselines as well as the trailing-30 mean. Confirmation requires BOTH: at or above the trailing local mean AND not materially below the session's established bucket rate. A bar that clears the local baseline while sitting under the session's own typical bucket is baseline collapse, not participation -- decline it and say which of the two it was.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.honest_scope: This changed no decision on the day it was found: the fire was declined on five independent merits (magnitude 0.044%, a mid-range level, both MAs overhead and untouched, ex-gap IV/RV 1.1697, no catalyst), and the follow-through reverted to 103% of baseline with price flat, so the trade was bad on the tape as well as on the filter. That is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly -- the same standard the 2026-08-25 calibration finding set for itself.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.class: Same family as every denominator finding in CLAUDE.md: a constant or a window encoded an assumption about a moving thing, nothing errored, and the wrong behaviour was indistinguishable from the right one. Here the assumption was that a locally-calibrated baseline is always the conservative choice. It is not; it is conservative in a rising tape and permissive in a draining one.

durable_findings.the_30_DTE_board_is_not_where_an_event_i: MEASURE THE EXPIRY THAT IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWS A PRINT BEFORE CLAIMING EVENT PREMIUM IS RISING -- iv_history's ~30-DTE method CANNOT see the event board, and this desk spent a full session citing the wrong one (measured 2026-08-26T16:20Z). The IV method deliberately reads the expiry nearest 30 DTE; that is correct for its purpose and must not be changed. But a 30-DTE board spanning an event blends event premium with ordinary positioning and dilutes the event across a much longer window, so its level is a poor proxy for what the market expects the event ITSELF to do. Measured on NVDA hours before its print: the 2026-08-28 210 straddle (the first expiry after the event) priced an implied move of +/-5.806% (12.20 on 210.135 spot) versus +/-5.975% from the prior session's settled closes (12.73 on 213.05) -- CONTRACTING -- while the 30-DTE board rose 0.4108 -> 0.4144 and every run that day called it 'event premium peaking into the print'. Front-board ATM IV 0.9488 vs 30-DTE 0.4144 is a 2.29x kink: the event lives on the front board, and only the front board answers 'what does the market expect this event to do'. DETECTOR, and it is two quotes: for any name with a known event inside the hold window, quote the ATM straddle on the FIRST expiry after the event and divide by spot; compare it to the SAME straddle's prior-session close. Rising = the event is being bid; flat or falling = expectations have stopped expanding regardless of what the 30-DTE row says. THE SHAPE, which is this file's most-repeated defect arriving through a new door: a correct measurement of the wrong board was allowed to answer a question it was never measuring, and nothing errored -- the conclusion was even right. Same family as the IV-sweep spread that became a liquidity verdict (2026-08-24) and the ATM quote that became an affordability verdict (2026-08-17). HONEST SCOPE: this changed no decision -- NVDA CORE is barred on the print, the exit engine and an n=12-record ex-gap ratio regardless -- which is the only condition under which auditing your own inputs is credible.
durable_findings.the_vacuum_reabsorbs_a_flush_within_minu: A GENUINE PARTICIPATION SPIKE IN A PRE-EVENT VACUUM DECAYS BACK TO THE VACUUM FASTER THAN A POSITION CAN BE MANAGED -- measured 2026-08-26T16:20Z, on the one bar all week that passed the two-sided volume test. The 16:01Z QQQ break bar printed 30,972 shares and the 16:00-16:09Z window averaged 21,588/min, clearing every denominator decisively; the very next window, 16:10-16:19Z, averaged 11,104/min = 51.4% of it. Price behaved identically: post-break low 708.777, then eighteen minutes oscillating 708.880-709.620, the last ten 1-minute closes spanning 0.29 points. NINE MINUTES from confirmed participation back to half-rate drift. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE OBVIOUS: the corrected volume clause (trailing-local baseline AND not materially below the session's earlier bucket rate) is designed to catch exactly this bar, and it DID -- the 16:00Z run recorded the fire honestly at 445.6% of trailing-30 and 248.4% of the session's own earlier buckets. The filter worked. What the filter cannot see is DURATION, and on a pre-event day the spike's half-life is shorter than a TACTICAL hold. So a passing volume reading in a vacuum session is a statement about one bar, not about the tape it opens into. Pair it with the 2026-08-26 durable finding on baseline collapse: in a draining tape the clause gets easier AND the participation it certifies is shorter-lived, and those two defects compound in the same direction. PRACTICAL RULE: on a session already measured as a pre-event vacuum, require the participation to PERSIST across at least the following window before sizing a scalp off it -- a fire whose volume reverts to baseline within one window has told you the flush was absorbed, not that a move started.

durable_findings.SPY_QQQ_leadership_inversion_2026-08-26: THE LEG THAT WAS 'HOLDING UP' IS THE ONE THAT BROKE. All session -- and in CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-24 tactical-band block -- SPY has been framed as the strong leg ('a low premium on the leg that is holding up is the same fact as this is the wrong leg to trade') and QQQ as the weak, Nasdaq-specific de-rating. Measured today at 16:45Z the frame is INVERTED: SPY lost a level it had defended since the opening minute (session low 764.680 == 20-day 764.7985) while QQQ did NOT make a new session low (707.970 stands; its lowest print since 14:28 is 708.290). The mechanism is not mysterious -- QQQ was ALREADY 3.70 below its 20-day and 4.55 below its 50-day, so it had no nearby level left to lose, whereas SPY still had one. TRANSFERABLE: 'which index is weaker on the day' and 'which index is breaking structure' are DIFFERENT QUESTIONS with different answers, and the tactical trigger cares only about the second. A name already far below its moving averages cannot generate an MA break; the name still sitting on one can. Ranking candidates by daily percentage change systematically points the hunt at the name LEAST likely to produce a fresh structural fire.
durable_findings.a_confirmed_trigger_is_not_a_tradeable_t: CHECK WHAT THE TARGET REQUIRES BEFORE TAKING A CONFIRMED BREAK -- this desk has spent two sessions calibrating whether a break is REAL and never once asked whether a real break at that level PAYS. Today's fire passed every filter the 2026-08-25/26 calibration work built (structural level not a desk-drawn box, completed close, held on following bars, volume clearing both the trailing-local and the session-rate denominators, index tape agreeing, chain 5x inside the liquidity gate, right delta, inside the size band) and was still not worth taking, because +20% required a 2.16-point SPY move against a 2.28-point session range with 3.1 hours left, and the best structural level on the chart paid only +18.5%. THE TEST, one line of arithmetic off the live greeks: solve the underlying move implied by the track's MINIMUM profit target, then compare it to (a) the session's realised range and (b) the distance to the next genuine structural level. If the minimum target needs more than roughly the session's whole range, or if reaching the best nearby level still misses the minimum target, DECLINE -- the level is too shallow to trade regardless of how cleanly it confirmed. This is the TACTICAL analogue of the CORE breakeven-scrutiny rule ('if the leg pays roughly nothing at the price where the thesis says to bank profit, skip it'), and the two should be read as one principle: a vehicle that is cheap, liquid and correctly triggered still supplies no edge if the payoff at the thesis target is not there. Note also WHY this nearly slipped through -- nineteen runs with no entry is precisely the condition under which a marginal setup gets upgraded, and a filter that has just been audited and PASSED feels like permission.
durable_findings.a_trigger_bar_can_pass_the_volume_test_w: TEST THE BARS THAT EXTEND THE MOVE, NOT ONLY THE BAR THAT FIRES IT -- measured 2026-08-26T17:15Z, on the session's first clean dual-denominator pass. This desk spent two sessions fixing the DENOMINATOR of the tactical volume clause (session-average too strict, 2026-08-25; trailing-local inverts in a decaying tape, 2026-08-26T15:52Z). Both fixes concern which baseline the CANDIDATE bar is measured against. Nobody had asked which BAR to measure. Measured on SPY's failed loss and reclaim of its 20-day SMA (764.798): the reclaim thrust 16:55-16:59 traded 31,420/min = 143.0% of the settled trailing-30 AND 131-168% of every earlier session bucket -- passing both halves, and genuinely not a baseline-collapse artifact. The continuation then FAILED the identical test: the hold 17:00-17:07 at 55.0% of trailing-30 and 50-65% of session buckets, and the extension 17:08-17:16 -- the bars carrying price 764.83 -> 765.45 to new highs -- at 82.3% of trailing-30 and 75.5-96.4% of every session bucket. Price made its high on the QUIETEST participation of the sequence. THE MECHANISM: a confirmed trigger bar proves that participation arrived AT THE LEVEL; it says nothing about whether participation STAYED for the move. A reclaim is exactly where that distinction bites, because the thrust is short-covering into the level and the drift afterward is nobody -- which is indistinguishable, from the trigger bar alone, from a real trend beginning. THE DETECTOR, one extra bucket of arithmetic already in hand: after a trigger passes, compute the same two ratios on the bars SINCE the fire. Confirmation requires participation at or above baseline on BOTH the trigger and the continuation; a passing trigger followed by sub-baseline extension is a fade setup, not a trend entry. HONEST SCOPE, same standard every calibration finding on this desk has held itself to: this changed NO decision today -- the fire was declined on three independent grounds (0.085% displacement past the level, smaller than the 0.106% declined on 08-25; NVDA at session lows contradicting the risk-appetite thesis; and the print tonight), so the audit is credible precisely because the answer did not turn on it. It also completes the family: the 2026-08-25 finding was that a filter rejecting everything must be audited on its baseline; this one is that a filter ACCEPTING something must be audited on what happens next.
